notes:
[Threads of Fate](item_cb61612b-9d83-49a9-989d-013bf084fbcb) provides the most consistent and reliable value for gathering cash in the first two rounds, and is also an excellent power for the entire rest of the match. It enables higher-skill-ceiling beam usage to increase your ability to help your teammates.

POWER TIPS:

The person receiving the chained beam will receive less healing, so when you need to heal two people at once, first flick your beam onto the person in less danger/who needs less healing, and then quickly switch to the person who needs the most healing. This way, the person in more danger will get more healing. 

The same concept applies for damage boosting. Make sure the main beam is on the person who's more likely to reach a damage breakpoint/get more value with the boost, and the chain beam is on the person who will get less value. 

Before each round starts, you can check your team's powers and items to see if they change which people are the most important to damage boost. For example, someone who you want to enable to carry, like a dynamite build Ashe, is extra important. Powers that already change round 1 breakpoints are also very important to boost, like a Freja with [Seekerpoint](item_7174fb2f-38d3-48d4-8705-5d90ac72876e). Giving a teammate unexpected lethality can have major impact.

The chained thread goes through walls and has no distance limitations--it will stay attached to the chained target for three seconds, no matter what. You can use this to get a lot of value with good beam management:

- If someone is about to go into an unsafe position where you will not be able to reach them, quickly put your beam on them before they leave. (For example, a Genji about to dash in, or a teleporting Reaper, or a charging Rein, etc.) To maximize the connection time, stay attached to them until the beam breaks. Then, flick your beam onto someone still near you. This way, you can give the person who's diving in a chained damage boost beam, and/or a bit of healing. 

- When doing the above, make sure that you connect your main beam to the person near you who most needs it. If you attach it to someone who doesn't need it as much, you might have to switch targets before the 3s is up, prematurely removing the chain beam from the far-off teammate. 

(Additionally, be careful in general not to accidentally connect to an unintended target and then mess up your desired chain beam--this is very frustrating to accidentally do in busy fights.)

- Since the beam has no distance limitations, you can fly partially to a teammate in an unreachable location, attach the beam, bounce back to your safe position, and then (like in the prior bulletpoint) proc the chain after the main beam connection breaks. This can often be repeated many times in a row to assist your split teammate. 

Don't forget to keep the threads always active so you can maximize your healing, or maximize your damage boost if everyone is full HP.

Sadly, threads does not work while valking. So if you ult, make sure you don't try to heal someone who's split from the team with threads and accidentally leave them without any beam. You'll have to heal them the old fashioned way.


Items:  

[Weapon Grease](item_961ae72f-434f-406b-a89b-ab8efec806bf) and  [Compensator](item_2a354f80-610c-4661-9bdd-8960ae1a60b0) give you the maximum healing output possible for round one. 

I prefer  [First Aid Kit](item_0172eaaa-1902-44a3-b989-d12f0f7301da) to  [Armored Vest](item_358361e2-59be-4c81-b221-8a87f37809e6) because 25 armor honestly is not very much, but  [First Aid Kit](item_0172eaaa-1902-44a3-b989-d12f0f7301da) makes it take only 2 seconds for Mercy to start passively regenerating HP instead of 3. This works well with Mercy's pre-existing playstyle of darting from safe position to safe position, and can allow you to increase your uptime by getting your HP resource back faster. Armored Vest is okay as well, but I suggest giving First Aid Kit a try if you've never used it before.

Pre-round notes:

In addition to checking your teammates' powers (as mentioned above), check the enemy powers/items after the armory phase ends and during the 10 second countdown. This is especially important on any round where new powers are unlocked, so you don't get caught off guard by power spikes or sudden changes. Be aware of the enemy powers and items that make someone a bigger threat to you/change breakpoints (e.g. S76's  [Super Visor](item_b3db0ab0-26b4-4d99-893d-175f6726c9e9) and  [Double Helix](item_808afc07-1398-4962-bf2c-f8e3b74014e3), Genji's  [Ambusher Optics](item_742c3c71-17cd-4fa7-bf18-ddeae7d521ca), D.Va's  [Dae-Hyun’s Detonator](item_cf3e51e1-12c7-4d92-a68b-7742f98fe8fa) and  [Express Detonation](item_8da4cbad-78cb-4ebd-8bc4-8dc150afec95), Freja's  [Seekerpoint](item_7174fb2f-38d3-48d4-8705-5d90ac72876e), and so much more.) 

Playstyle notes: 

Unlike in regular Overwatch, **you get a material benefit from greedy healbotting: Cash.** Instead of mindlessly using either beam as your default, look for opportunities to heal as much as possible, while still damage boosting at critical moments. (E.g. teammate getting a good angle on an unsuspecting enemy, teammate about to use an ability like dynamite, firestrike, orbs, dash, etc., teammate ulting, teammate trying to finish off low HP enemy, etc.)

You do still make cash from damage boosting, but it's far less than for healing. Why? Damage boost only gives you the cash for the amount of damage contributed by your amplification, which will be much less than what you get from healing. So **if you feel overwhelmed by trying to minmax your heal/boost usage, just focus more on healing.** 

And, **as a rule, if you feel like you're not making enough cash, try healing more, and boosting less.** 

The goal is to make enough cash that, later into the game, you can purchase high enough HPS to rapidly farm powerful boost-heavy  [Crepuscular Circle](item_c0b93ed2-b692-44d5-a38a-ce5a63e83cdb) ults. 

Remember to top off even little smidgens of missing HP you might ignore/let slide in the normal game. **Even when overtime is ticking down and the round is about to end, steal those last slivers of cash you can get right up until the round finish.**

As in the main game, try to prioritize dying as minimally as possible. If you're someone who really struggles with this,  [Winning Attitude](item_8714087c-c078-4619-a2ef-327bc6edaa69) could be your alternative to  [First Aid Kit](item_0172eaaa-1902-44a3-b989-d12f0f7301da), but you should never *plan* on dying.

Lastly, speaking of dying: If the round is over and you've 100% lost no matter what, fight your instincts, and *don't run onto the point to die anyway.* You'll avoid feeding the enemies that extra bit of cash. **This is especially important if you, at any point, have a bounty.**

I don't want to turn this into a generalized Mercy guide instead of a stadium-specific one, but I suggest that, if you really struggle not to die in stadium, you should check out normal Mercy guides for positioning/survival tips, instead of immediately leaping to always using 3+ survival items as a crutch. General skill on Mercy translates into playing well in stadium, and no single build can fully replace the benefits of having that skill.

I begin each round by selling all of my previous items so that I can more comfortably see how much cash I have to work with, even if I know I may buy some of them back. 

Option one:

My default. [Talon Modification Module](item_c0ca1795-a3ea-4dc9-ae17-f34122574b3a),  [Advanced Nanobiotics](item_26fcf7c9-b81a-4d8e-a459-b515519cb73e), and  [Aftermarket Firing Pin](item_2485b212-b286-42d0-a2bd-20eb4396b054). This gives an even 20 WP / 20AS ratio, which gives at least ~5 more HPS than 40 WP / 0 AS does, and is also much cheaper. 

(Remember,  [Advanced Nanobiotics](item_26fcf7c9-b81a-4d8e-a459-b515519cb73e)'s AS buff will always be active for Mercy, so you have 20 AS even though the stat bar only shows 10. It also provides a nice move speed bonus.) 

Option two:

If you have a lot of money, you can buy all 3 of the listed blues, keep both  [Compensator](item_2a354f80-610c-4661-9bdd-8960ae1a60b0) and  [Weapon Grease](item_961ae72f-434f-406b-a89b-ab8efec806bf), and maybe even keep your  [First Aid Kit](item_0172eaaa-1902-44a3-b989-d12f0f7301da). This option has the highest HPS out of the three.

Option three:

The cheapest set-up is  [Advanced Nanobiotics](item_26fcf7c9-b81a-4d8e-a459-b515519cb73e),  [Mid-Air Mobilizer](item_760c1441-8cfa-426c-885d-8d0dec32e145),  [Compensator](item_2a354f80-610c-4661-9bdd-8960ae1a60b0), and  [Weapon Grease](item_961ae72f-434f-406b-a89b-ab8efec806bf). This option is ~3 HPS more than option one, but ~3 HPS less than option two. However, it only has more HPS than option one while you're midair. When not midair, it provides ~3-5 less HPS than option one.

[Mid-Air Mobilizer](item_760c1441-8cfa-426c-885d-8d0dec32e145) *is* very easy to trigger--it works while you're GA'ing, and while you're any distance above the ground more than just a regular jump. However, the item does often require extra hassle to use without engaging in unsafe positioning.

This option is highly recommended if you are against a team without any hitscans, or if you're very low-cash. If the enemy team does have hitscans and you need to take this option regardless, suggestions/tips are:

- Keep yourself consistently in the air via high superjumps behind cover (only when the enemy can't easily/immediately rotate to catch you out!).

- When there is no good cover for high superjumps, perform consistent small superjumps in as much cover as possible. 

- Use angelic descent to prolong air time without having to constantly spam GA.

- Be careful not to waste a GA on staying in the air when you'll need it to escape. Remember that regular GAs will also proc mid-air mobilizer, so you can also simply fly back and forth/fly around in safe ways to proc it regularly. Superjumps are only for when you have no other place to fly, and would normally be on the ground.

- You always count as 'mid-air' in valk, even if you're pressed to the floor. 

Low cash/miscellaneous item selections:

If things are going very badly and you have very little cash, or if you have an odd amount of cash, be aware that  [Advanced Nanobiotics](item_26fcf7c9-b81a-4d8e-a459-b515519cb73e) does a few more HPS than  [Talon Modification Module](item_c0ca1795-a3ea-4dc9-ae17-f34122574b3a), so you should prioritize it. 

You can mix in miscellaneous green survival items if you have spare cash that you can't put towards a HPS item (that is, if you already have compensator/weapon grease but can't afford another blue).  [First Aid Kit](item_0172eaaa-1902-44a3-b989-d12f0f7301da) and  [Armored Vest](item_358361e2-59be-4c81-b221-8a87f37809e6) are the spare 1.5k options, and I like  [Running Shoes](item_950eccea-31a0-4a55-8c2a-75bf7920e1aa) as the spare 1k option because it's the only 1k item that gives you HP + it lets you run back faster from spawn if you die. You could also take  [Charged Plating](item_b8ca58e7-6ae2-40ee-8618-fe2f32315295), but only getting the 25 armor after you ult isn't worth it to me. 

Other misc. note: I recommend only buying the survival items *if* you have spare/odd cash. **It's important to maximize your healing this round, and continue focusing on cash gathering.** Good positioning + sympathetic recovery can keep you alive even without any green survival items.

Power:  [Crepuscular Circle](item_c0b93ed2-b692-44d5-a38a-ce5a63e83cdb) is a must-have. It transforms valk from one of the most mediocre ults in the game into what is, at this point, already a better orbital ray. (It's almost 2x as long, has higher HPS that will keep scaling, also gives the constant damage boost, and can be charged much, much quicker.) 

- Crepuscular Circle beams all reach very far, no beam chaining needed. Even in a split teamfight, if you find the right place to float, you can give your entire team the benefit of the ult. 

- While you can now use your gun while valk is active, your sympathetic recovery HPS isn't very high yet, and your gun isn't especially buffed. Be careful not to get too greedy and accidentally get yourself killed trying to shoot people. Since the ult is so powerful, it's very important not to get it ended early. 

- Also, be careful not to get so focused on getting kills that you accidentally leave LoS of your teammates and abandon them. Stay aware of where you are. 

- Remember that you can now rez while ulting without your team losing out on any heals (unless LoS is lost). It can be great to pop ult to get away with a rez whilst buffing the rest of your team. 

- This is more general advice, but track your team's ults, and if they have a lot, consider waiting a moment before valking to see if they'll instantly use them all to win the teamfight. If this happens and you've saved your ult, you'll have a powerful ult that might allow your team to recuperate when the enemy team comes back with all *their* ults. The damage boost you apply with Crepuscular Circle is also great for helping your teammates recharge their ults. 

For items:

Replace [Talon Modification Module](item_c0ca1795-a3ea-4dc9-ae17-f34122574b3a) with  [Amari's Antidote](item_67e0b1c5-3bcb-4ab5-b818-5082e5706124). You may already know this, but rather than just counting as an extra 15% WP when healing teammates below half HP, Amari's Antidote actually adds 15% *multiplicative* healing value. As one test showed:

- 75% WP without Amari's gives 107 HPS. 

- 90% WP (15% more WP than 75%) without Amari's gives 113 HPS. 

- But, 75% WP with Amari's gives 123 HPS, not 113.

As a result, Amari's Antidote is an excellent item. I've noticed that taking it round 3 makes it far easier to keep my team alive than if I don't. And, since it's multiplicative, it will only become more valuable as the game goes on.

Round three is also the first power spike, so it's very risky to go without taking any survival items--taking some damage is inevitable no matter *how* good you are at positioning, and when that damage is scaled up, your tankiness needs to be scaled to match.  [Vital-E-Tee](item_b92e6f1d-3aac-4eec-b027-00c8e1529016) is a good choice for making you flat-out tankier without breaking the bank. 

If you don't have enough cash for this, you can mix and match in some of the optional items to get the highest WP/AS + survivability ratio possible with your purchasing power. If you feel comfortable doing so, prioritize the weapon items, and replace  [Crusader Hydraulics](item_b64cee07-ca32-405d-987e-868b415bbc09) with green survival items. If you already really struggled to survive in rounds 1 and 2, prioritize  [Crusader Hydraulics](item_b64cee07-ca32-405d-987e-868b415bbc09) over the ideal weapon items.

Playstyle notes:

Remember to check your team/the enemy team's new powers this round, especially the enemy's, so you don't get caught off guard.

As everyone's builds scale, TTK can become much shorter over the course of the game. This is especially prominent in lobbies where your team is failing to build enough survival for themselves. This means that, starting now--and as the game goes on--**you will need to have increasingly high awareness of which teammates are in danger, and fast reaction times for getting your beam onto them.** Your HPS will become high, but a single second could be the difference between you saving someone, and them dying before you ever get your beam onto them. So be ready to be alert!

Items:

Option one: Replace  [Aftermarket Firing Pin](item_2485b212-b286-42d0-a2bd-20eb4396b054) with  [Booster Jets](item_a291de85-b6d9-43cf-b5da-f3184a156f48) and repurchase  [Talon Modification Module](item_c0ca1795-a3ea-4dc9-ae17-f34122574b3a) and  [Weapon Grease](item_961ae72f-434f-406b-a89b-ab8efec806bf). This gives ~126 HPS max.

Option two: If you can afford most of the above option, but barely don't have enough to include  [Weapon Grease](item_961ae72f-434f-406b-a89b-ab8efec806bf), it will only do ~119 HPS max. 

Option three:  [Amari's Antidote](item_67e0b1c5-3bcb-4ab5-b818-5082e5706124),  [Booster Jets](item_a291de85-b6d9-43cf-b5da-f3184a156f48),  [Advanced Nanobiotics](item_26fcf7c9-b81a-4d8e-a459-b515519cb73e), and  [Mid-Air Mobilizer](item_760c1441-8cfa-426c-885d-8d0dec32e145) will give you ~123 HPS max while mid-air. 

I recommend trying to take option one if possible. If you take option three, the previously stated tips about mid-air mobilizer apply. Option three is preferred over option two, since it has more HPS. You can also mix and match your own selections of items to try to maximize your WP/AS ratio with the amount of survivability you're comfortable with.

Miscellaneous mid-game items:

Assuming the MMR of the lobby is reasonably balanced, the ideal build set-up should be working reasonably well for you. However, if different circumstances require you to adapt, this is the point in the game to start considering what items you'll adapt with. 

I know that you probably won't have enough money to rush these now, but round four is what I'd consider to be the start of the mid-game. So, I'm listing these here, and you can purchase one now if you're able, in round five, or in round six, depending on when you have enough money, and when you feel you need it.

If the enemy team is successfully diving you with a less hitscan-centric comp, or if you have a very mobile teammate that you need to help but can't easily follow: Replace  [Vital-E-Tee](item_b92e6f1d-3aac-4eec-b027-00c8e1529016)  with  [Blessed Boosters](item_957fd380-b7b4-40d4-8333-bb8c535ca931) 

If you feel like you can't attach your beam to teammates without peeking deadly hitscans, or if you feel like you need to be positioned farther away from the dangers of teamfights: Swap  [Talon Modification Module](item_c0ca1795-a3ea-4dc9-ae17-f34122574b3a) or another WP item for [Caduceus Ex](item_9e7965ea-2abc-44a7-b042-950c6ad2fce7) 

If you feel like you have a competent team that's really utilizing damage boost: Replace [Vital-E-Tee](item_b92e6f1d-3aac-4eec-b027-00c8e1529016)  with  [Chain Evoker](item_812cc89e-feb0-47d0-9e03-9d8e33a80aca) 

If you are just absolutely getting murdered/oneshot, to the extent where you can't heal or exist outside of spawn, you can sacrifice HPS for a wide variety of survival items:

- [Nebula Conduit](item_476b7040-54c9-4f0c-8283-b4407f6809f8) and [Divine Intervention](item_b5148b7f-8529-4b1b-a90c-5d7cf13f8f0c) are good against high burst damage

-  [Crusader Hydraulics](item_b64cee07-ca32-405d-987e-868b415bbc09) +  [Vital-E-Tee](item_b92e6f1d-3aac-4eec-b027-00c8e1529016) and/or  [Iron Eyes](item_f16d03a7-f20e-4a1d-a1f6-55863e163c03) are good against high WP (although try taking  [Caduceus Ex](item_9e7965ea-2abc-44a7-b042-950c6ad2fce7) first, if you're against non-mobile hitscans that you can theoretically avoid LoS of)

-  [Cushioned Padding](item_20f2f4bc-4611-4d1f-b653-20f04d56b96f) is good into sleep/anti/burn/etc

-  [Vishkar Condensor](item_086a91da-b65d-4047-8fc7-28a992078b1d) and  [Reinforced Titanium](item_8ebaa7db-aedf-48ed-adc1-318cb46a3214) are good against ability damage

- And of course, there's whatever other items you find useful/comfortable 

Playstyle:

Your healing is beginning to really scale, now, and so is the enemy team's damage. While you should continue to use damage boost intelligently for the whole game, keep in mind that you can now begin to farm valk rather quickly with healbotting. Valk is so powerful that it's really worth pushing for quickly. You can look for some kills, within reason.

At this point, you may have enough cash for the full build in some games, although it's likely you won't depending on the match. If you don't have enough, just build the highest ratio of WP to AS possible + any desired mid-game items, and then purchase the endgame items next round.

However, since you *can* have enough cash in some games, and our third power comes online now, I'll explain the end-game build here.

( [Serenity](item_c6e1c072-ff50-467e-b59f-9506baea10c1) can be taken instead of  [Battle Medic](item_ccd0edff-4d57-4ac2-83a7-bab6ff0ffb2f) if you're having to diverge into a tankier build as mentioned in round four's "If you're getting murdered" section. If you take Serenity here, you'll have to wait until round 7 for max possible HPS.)

A unique, unintended power interaction occurs here. Rather than applying extra AS to your gun specifically,  [Battle Medic](item_ccd0edff-4d57-4ac2-83a7-bab6ff0ffb2f) applies extra AS to *you as a whole* any time you have your gun out. (You don't have to be shooting, just whenever you have your gun out.) Normally, you can't heal while your gun is out, so your HPS can never benefit from the AS buff.

But, when you have  [Crepuscular Circle](item_c0b93ed2-b692-44d5-a38a-ce5a63e83cdb), you *can* heal while your gun is out. This means that, during ult, Battle Medic's AS buff applies to your healing as well. 

You can also use Battle Medic while valking to easily shoot enemies and proc  [Weapon Jammer](item_72386db6-753e-413d-aa2a-f1389842f47f), which gives you even more AS for two seconds after you've dealt damage to an enemy.

As a result, these are what the possible healing numbers look like, on targets below 50% HP (Amari's applies) and above 50% HP (Amari's will not apply). 

Raw healing out of valk:

- Above 50% hp grants roughly 133 HPS

- Below 50% hp grants roughly 153 HPS

In valk:

No battle medic and no weapon jammer proc:

- Above 50% hp grants roughly 144 HPS

- Below 50% hp grants roughly 166 HPS

Yes battle medic proc but no weapon jammer proc:

 - Above 50% hp grants roughly 182 HPS

- Below 50% hp grants roughly 213 HPS

Yes battle medic and yes weapon jammer proc:

- Above 50% hp grants roughly 195 HPS

- Below 50% hp grants roughly 225 HPS

The final playstyle is to farm valk as fast as possible through healbotting, and then target the most vulnerable enemy for assassination--doing massive healing and solid damage simultaneously.

 [Battle Medic](item_ccd0edff-4d57-4ac2-83a7-bab6ff0ffb2f) Tips: 

- Even if you can't kill a zippy enemy Mercy, bullying her in valk can force her into bad positions where a teammate can finish her off, or discourage her from rezzing/helping teammates. 

- Same rules as looking for kills w/ valk in normal overwatch apply--relatively stationary, low hp, or distracted targets are vulnerable. To paraphrase some advice from the youtube video linked in the build description: You don't need amazing aim so long as you just quickly get into close range and drill people with your bullets. 

- If you can't find any other more high-value targets, or you're really having a bad time aiming, it can work fine to just harass the enemy tank. You can get a surprisingly decent chunk of damage in, distract/disorient them (especially Reins trying to shield), and constantly proc your max HPS.

- If you can't find anyone to shoot at all, still keep your gun out, since that will give you the bonus AS stacks.
If you weren't able to afford the endgame build last round, you should be able to obtain it now. The same explanation/tips as last round apply here.

Finally, if you don't have it already, taking  [Serenity](item_c6e1c072-ff50-467e-b59f-9506baea10c1) is good insurance for keeping yourself alive during the end-game power spike. My approach here is that you're already going to be easily keeping your team alive, so you don't need to invest a further power into them. Instead, invest a power into keeping *yourself* alive through any mistakes or surprises, so that you can be there for all the critical moments. 

(If you already took Serenity, take  [Battle Medic](item_ccd0edff-4d57-4ac2-83a7-bab6ff0ffb2f) instead, so you can proc the max HPS as explained in round five.)

Round seven often has very lengthy, stall-y fights. Keep healbotting to valk and then utilizing battle medic to do damage/get kills. Use Serenity and solid positioning to ensure you don't ever die this round. So long as you're alive and getting valks, it's likely your team will be able to outlast the enemies.
